transformNotes: Rows of ECDICT ecdict.csv whose 'tag' column contains cet4 / cet6 respectively; one word pack per level. 'meanings' comes from splitting the source 'translation' cell on newlines (a literal backslash-n in a few rows is treated as a newline too). A leading part-of-speech marker (n. / v. / vt. / vi. / a. / adv. ...) is removed from the meaning text and recorded in 'partOfSpeech' only when the whole entry uses exactly one distinct marker; entries with mixed markers keep their text verbatim, marker included. 'phonetic' is the source 'phonetic' column with one leading and trailing slash added when absent; ECDICT carries a single transcription, so phoneticUs and phoneticUk are empty strings and 'phonetic' holds that single value. ECDICT has no example sentences, no collocations and no separate US/UK phonetics, so those fields are empty rather than invented. Rows with an empty word or an empty translation were dropped; case-insensitive duplicates inside one list kept the richest row. 'id' is level + 1-based index in the emitted order. Example sentences are a second stage (tools/wordpack/attach_examples.py): one Tatoeba sentence per word, selected for readability and never invented. Words with no acceptable sentence keep an empty example field; the app hides an empty example instead of faking one. examples.selection: One sentence per word: exact form preferred over a regular inflection; Simplified Chinese preferred (Traditional converted with the OpenCC tables); fewest out-of-vocabulary tokens against CET-4/CET-6 + an ECDICT frequency core + function words; no proper names; shortest sentence wins; longest Tatoeba id as tie-break.
